title: Decimals: Tenths and Hundredths, Fractions and Money
seo_title: Grade 4 Decimals Worksheets: Tenths, Hundredths and Money (TEKS 4.2E, 4.2G, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.2E represent decimals, including tenths and hundredths, using concrete and visual models and money; 4.2G relate decimals to fractions that name tenths and hundredths
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 decimal worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.2E and 4.2G: tenths bars and hundredths grids, fractions and decimals, decimal place value, money as decimals and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The first place after the point is tenths, the second is hundredths. A dime is $0.10 and a penny is $0.01.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A tenth is 1 of 10 equal parts: 0.1 = 1/10. A hundredth is 1 of 100 equal parts: 0.01 = 1/100.
  • The first place after the decimal point is tenths; the second is hundredths. 0.47 is 4 tenths and 7 hundredths, or 47 hundredths.
  • Money uses hundredths of a dollar: a dime is $0.10 and a penny is $0.01.

Examples

Example

Write 7/100 as a decimal.

7 hundredths

The hundredths place is the second place after the point.

Answer: 0.07

Example

3 dimes and 4 pennies

30¢ + 4¢ = 34¢

34 hundredths of a dollar

Answer: $0.34

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 7/100 as 0.70.7 is 7 tenths. 7 hundredths is 0.07.
Reading 0.5 as 5 hundredths0.5 = 5 tenths = 50 hundredths.
Writing 3 dimes as $0.03A dime is a tenth of a dollar: $0.30.

faq.a: Represent decimals, including tenths and hundredths, using concrete and visual models and money.
Relate decimals to fractions that name tenths and hundredths, such as 0.3 = 3/10 and 0.25 = 25/100.
Yes. 5 tenths is the same amount as 50 hundredths.

faq.q: How does money help with decimals?
faq.a: A dollar is the whole. Dimes are tenths and pennies are hundredths, so $0.47 is 4 dimes and 7 pennies.

sets.title: Read tenths bars and hundredths grids

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth and each full column is 1 tenth. 4 full columns and 7 squares are shaded: 4 tenths and 7 hundredths. That is 47100 = 0.47.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth. Only 8 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 8 hundredths = 8100 = 0.08.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth and each full column is 1 tenth. 6 full columns and 2 squares are shaded: 6 tenths and 2 hundredths. That is 62100 = 0.62.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth and each full column is 1 tenth. 1 full column and 5 squares are shaded: 1 tenth and 5 hundredths. That is 15100 = 0.15.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth. Only 3 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 3 hundredths = 3100 = 0.03.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth and each full column is 1 tenth. 9 full columns and 1 square are shaded: 9 tenths and 1 hundredth. That is 91100 = 0.91.

items.q: What decimal names the shaded part of the grid?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, so each square is 1 hundredth and each full column is 1 tenth. 5 full columns and 6 squares are shaded: 5 tenths and 6 hundredths. That is 56100 = 0.56.

items.q: What fraction of the grid is shaded? Use hundredths.
items.e: Count the shaded squares: 30 squares out of 100 equal squares. The fraction is 30100. The bottom number is all 100 squares, not the white ones. (It is also 310, because 3 full columns are shaded.)

items.q: What fraction of the grid is shaded? Use hundredths.
items.e: Count the shaded squares: 24 squares out of 100 equal squares. The fraction is 24100. The bottom number is all 100 squares, not the white ones.

items.q: What fraction of the grid is shaded? Use hundredths.
items.e: Count the shaded squares: 9 squares out of 100 equal squares. The fraction is 9100. The bottom number is all 100 squares, not the white ones.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 7 parts are shaded: 710 = 0.7. One digit after the point means tenths.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 3 parts are shaded: 310 = 0.3. One digit after the point means tenths.

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What fraction is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts and 9 are shaded, so the shaded part is 910 (0.9).

items.q: The whole bar is 1. What fraction is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts and 4 are shaded, so the shaded part is 410 (0.4).

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. What decimal names the shaded part?
items.e: Each grid is 1 whole. The first grid is all shaded: 1 whole. The second grid has 25 hundredths = 0.25. Together: 1 and 25 hundredths = 1.25.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. What decimal names the shaded part?
items.e: Each grid is 1 whole. The first grid is all shaded: 1 whole. The second grid has 6 hundredths = 0.06. Together: 1 and 6 hundredths = 1.06.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.4?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.4 = 40100, so shade 40 squares. 4 tenths is the same as 40 hundredths: 4 full columns.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.35?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.35 = 35100, so shade 35 squares.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.09?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.09 = 9100, so shade 9 squares. The 0 in the tenths place means no full column.

items.q: How many squares of a hundredths grid should you shade to show 0.72?
items.e: A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so you need the number of hundredths. 0.72 = 72100, so shade 72 squares.

items.q: A long jump is 2 and 810 meters. Which decimal shows this?
items.e: 2 and 8 tenths is 2.8.

items.q: A long jump is 4 and 510 meters. Which decimal shows this?
items.e: 4 and 5 tenths is 4.5.

items.q: Write 110 as a decimal.
items.e: 110 is 1 tenth: 0.1.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.16?
items.e: 0.16 is 16 hundredths: 16100.

items.q: 810 is equal to how many hundredths?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 810 = 80100 = 0.80.

items.q: 110 is equal to how many hundredths?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 110 = 10100 = 0.10.

items.q: A long jump is 1 and 510 meters. Which decimal shows this?
items.e: 1 and 5 tenths is 1.5.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.98?
items.e: 0.98 is 98 hundredths: 98100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.46?
items.e: 0.46 is 46 hundredths: 46100.

items.q: 910 is equal to how many hundredths?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 910 = 90100 = 0.90.

items.q: A long jump is 8 and 810 meters. Which decimal shows this?
items.e: 8 and 8 tenths is 8.8.

items.q: A long jump is 5 and 110 meters. Which decimal shows this?
items.e: 5 and 1 tenth is 5.1.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.58?
items.e: 0.58 is 58 hundredths: 58100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.89?
items.e: 0.89 is 89 hundredths: 89100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.45?
items.e: 0.45 is 45 hundredths: 45100.

items.q: 310 is equal to how many hundredths?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 310 = 30100 = 0.30.

items.q: A long jump is 9 and 810 meters. Which decimal shows this?
items.e: 9 and 8 tenths is 9.8.

items.q: A long jump is 1 and 210 meters. Which decimal shows this?
items.e: 1 and 2 tenths is 1.2.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.63?
items.e: 0.63 is 63 hundredths: 63100.

items.q: Write 510 as a decimal.
items.e: 510 is 5 tenths: 0.5.

items.q: Write 7100 as a decimal.
items.e: 7100 means 7 hundredths. Hundredths need two digits after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.07. (0.7 would be 7 tenths.)

items.q: Write 45100 as a decimal.
items.e: 45100 means 45 hundredths: 4 tenths and 5 hundredths. The hundredths digit goes in the second place after the point: 0.45.

items.q: Write 3100 as a decimal.
items.e: 3100 means 3 hundredths. Hundredths need two digits after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.03. (0.3 would be 3 tenths.)

items.q: Write 80100 as a decimal.
items.e: 80100 = 0.8, because 80 hundredths is the same as 8 tenths. Both name the same point: 0.80 = 0.8.

items.q: Write 16100 as a decimal.
items.e: 16100 means 16 hundredths: 1 tenth and 6 hundredths. The hundredths digit goes in the second place after the point: 0.16.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 has one digit after the point, so it means 6 tenths: 610.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.09?
items.e: 0.09 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. 0.09 = 9 hundredths, which is 9100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.32?
items.e: 0.32 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. 0.32 = 32 hundredths, which is 32100.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.05?
items.e: 0.05 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. 0.05 = 5 hundredths, which is 5100.

items.q: 310 = ?100
items.e: To go from tenths to hundredths, cut each tenth into 10 hundredths. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 310 = 30100. The bottom number grew by ×10, so the top number must too.

items.q: 710 = ?100
items.e: To go from tenths to hundredths, cut each tenth into 10 hundredths. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 710 = 70100. The bottom number grew by ×10, so the top number must too.

items.q: 510 = ?100
items.e: To go from tenths to hundredths, cut each tenth into 10 hundredths. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 510 = 50100. The bottom number grew by ×10, so the top number must too.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 0.7?
items.e: 0.7 is 7 tenths. 7 tenths = 70 hundredths, so 0.7 = 0.70. A 0 at the end does not change the value. A 0 right after the point does: 0.07 is only 7 hundredths.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 0.58?
items.e: The 8 is the second digit after the point, the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths (0.08).

items.q: What is the value of the 6 in 4.63?
items.e: The 6 is the first digit after the point, the tenths place. Its value is 6 tenths (0.6). Tens are on the left of the ones; tenths are on the right of the point.

items.q: Which digit is in the hundredths place in 17.35?
items.e: Places after the point: tenths first (3), then hundredths (5). The 1 is in the tens place, not the hundreds place.

items.q: Which digit is in the tenths place in 52.86?
items.e: The tenths place is the first digit after the point: 8. The 5 is in the tens place, on the other side of the point.

items.q: Which decimal is thirty-six hundredths?
items.e: Hundredths means two digits after the point: 36 hundredths = 36100 = 0.36.

items.q: Which decimal is two and five tenths?
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. 2 wholes and 5 tenths: 2.5. (2.05 would be 5 hundredths.)

items.q: Which decimal is four and seven hundredths?
items.e: 4 wholes, then the point. 7 hundredths needs two places, so put a 0 in the tenths place: 4.07.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 9 dollar bills, 3 quarters, 4 nickels.
items.e: The coins make 95¢, which is 95 hundredths of a dollar. $9.95.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 9 dollar bills, 3 quarters, 1 penny.
items.e: The coins make 76¢, which is 76 hundredths of a dollar. $9.76.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 9 dollar bills, 2 nickels, 1 dime.
items.e: The coins make 20¢, which is 20 hundredths of a dollar. $9.20.

items.q: What part of a dollar is 3¢, written as a decimal?
items.e: 3¢ is 3100 of a dollar, so it is $0.03.

items.q: Gabriel has 4 dimes and 8 pennies. Which decimal shows how much money that is in dollars?
items.e: A dime is one tenth of a dollar and a penny is one hundredth. 4 tenths and 8 hundredths is 0.48.

items.q: Emma has 2 dimes and 4 pennies. Which decimal shows how much money that is in dollars?
items.e: A dime is one tenth of a dollar and a penny is one hundredth. 2 tenths and 4 hundredths is 0.24.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 2 dollar bills, 4 quarters.
items.e: The coins make 100¢, which is 100 hundredths of a dollar. $3.00.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 2 dollar bills, 4 pennies.
items.e: The coins make 4¢, which is 4 hundredths of a dollar. $2.04.

items.q: Isabella has 9 dimes and 7 pennies. Which decimal shows how much money that is in dollars?
items.e: A dime is one tenth of a dollar and a penny is one hundredth. 9 tenths and 7 hundredths is 0.97.

items.q: Grace has 7 dimes and 1 penny. Which decimal shows how much money that is in dollars?
items.e: A dime is one tenth of a dollar and a penny is one hundredth. 7 tenths and 1 hundredth is 0.71.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 3 dollar bills, 3 pennies, 2 dimes.
items.e: The coins make 23¢, which is 23 hundredths of a dollar. $3.23.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 3 nickels.
items.e: The coins make 15¢, which is 15 hundredths of a dollar. $0.15.

items.q: Zoe has 2 dimes and 1 penny. Which decimal shows how much money that is in dollars?
items.e: A dime is one tenth of a dollar and a penny is one hundredth. 2 tenths and 1 hundredth is 0.21.

items.q: Luis has 1 dime and 3 pennies. Which decimal shows how much money that is in dollars?
items.e: A dime is one tenth of a dollar and a penny is one hundredth. 1 tenth and 3 hundredths is 0.13.

items.q: Mateo has 4 dimes and 5 pennies. Which decimal shows how much money that is in dollars?
items.e: A dime is one tenth of a dollar and a penny is one hundredth. 4 tenths and 5 hundredths is 0.45.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 2 dollar bills, 4 dimes, 4 quarters.
items.e: The coins make 140¢, which is 140 hundredths of a dollar. $3.40.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 5 dollar bills, 4 nickels, 1 quarter.
items.e: The coins make 45¢, which is 45 hundredths of a dollar. $5.45.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 5 dollar bills, 2 quarters, 4 pennies.
items.e: The coins make 54¢, which is 54 hundredths of a dollar. $5.54.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 9 dollar bills, 2 pennies.
items.e: The coins make 2¢, which is 2 hundredths of a dollar. $9.02.

items.q: Write the amount as a decimal of a dollar: 6 dollar bills, 2 pennies.
items.e: The coins make 2¢, which is 2 hundredths of a dollar. $6.02.

items.q: A dime is 110 of a dollar and a penny is 1100 of a dollar. Liam has 3 dimes and 4 pennies. How much money does he have?
items.e: 3 dimes = 310, 4 pennies = 4100. In all: 34100 of a dollar = $0.34. Count the value, not the number of coins.

items.q: A dime is 110 of a dollar and a penny is 1100 of a dollar. Isaac has 5 dimes. How much money does he have?
items.e: 5 dimes = 510 = 50100 of a dollar = $0.50. 5 tenths = 50 hundredths, which is 50 cents.

items.q: A dime is 110 of a dollar and a penny is 1100 of a dollar. Sofia has 1 dime and 8 pennies. How much money does she have?
items.e: 1 dime = 110, 8 pennies = 8100. In all: 18100 of a dollar = $0.18. Count the value, not the number of coins.

items.q: Nevaeh wants to pay $0.85 with only dimes and pennies, using the fewest coins. Which coins does she use?
items.e: $0.85 = 8 tenths and 5 hundredths. A dime is a tenth and a penny is a hundredth: 8 dimes and 5 pennies. 85 pennies is also $0.85, but it uses many more coins.

items.q: Caleb has 4 dimes. He finds 25 pennies. How much money does he have now?
items.e: 4 dimes = 410 = 40100. Add the pennies: 40100 + 25100 = 65100 = $0.65. Do not add 4 and 25: a dime is worth 10 pennies.

items.q: Mateo has 6 dimes. Ximena has 5 dimes and 8 pennies. Who has more money?
items.e: Mateo has $0.60. Ximena has $0.58. 60 cents is more than 58 cents, so Mateo has more, even though Ximena has more coins.

items.q: How many pennies make 0.3 of a dollar?
items.e: 0.3 = 310 = 30100. A penny is 1 hundredth of a dollar, so you need 30 pennies (30 cents).

items.q: A plant grew 0.3 meter in spring and 0.25 meter in summer. How much did it grow in all?
items.e: 0.3 = 30100. Add hundredths to hundredths: 30100 + 25100 = 55100 = 0.55 m. Line up the tenths with the tenths.

items.q: Aaliyah jumped 1.4 meters. Harper jumped 1.35 meters. Who jumped farther?
items.e: Both jumped 1 whole meter. Compare the tenths: 1.4 has 4 tenths, 1.35 has 3 tenths. 1.4 = 1.40 > 1.35, so Aaliyah jumped farther. More digits does not mean bigger.

items.q: Three pencils are 0.15 m, 0.2 m and 0.12 m long. Which pencil is the shortest?
items.e: Write all as hundredths: 0.15 = 15, 0.2 = 20, 0.12 = 12 hundredths. The shortest is 0.12 m. 0.2 is not the shortest: 2 tenths is 20 hundredths.

items.q: Diego ate 0.5 of a small pizza. Lucia ate 0.4 of a large pizza. Diego says he ate more because 0.5 > 0.4. Is he right?
items.e: You can compare decimals only when they are parts of the same whole. Half of a small pizza can be less than 0.4 of a large pizza, so Diego cannot be sure.

items.q: Two water bottles are the same size. One is 0.8 full. The other is 0.75 full. Which has more water?
items.e: The bottles are the same size, so you can compare. 0.8 = 0.80, and 80 hundredths > 75 hundredths. The 0.8 bottle has more.

items.q: A garden has 100 equal plots. Tomatoes grow in 23 of them. What decimal names the part with tomatoes?
items.e: 23 out of 100 equal plots is 23100 = 0.23.

items.q: A class has 10 students. 7 of them walk to school. What decimal names the part of the class that walks?
items.e: 7 out of 10 students is 710. Tenths have one digit after the point: 0.7. (0.3 is the part that does not walk.)

items.q: A recipe needs 0.5 liter of milk and 0.25 liter of cream. How much is that in all?
items.e: 0.5 = 510 = 50100. Then 50100 + 25100 = 75100 = 0.75 L. Add tenths to tenths and hundredths to hundredths.

items.q: A meter has 100 centimeters. A crayon is 9 centimeters long. How long is it in meters?
items.e: Each centimeter is 1100 of a meter. 9 centimeters = 9100 = 0.09 m. (0.9 m would be 90 centimeters.)

items.q: Mia says 0.3 = 0.30. Is she right?
items.e: 0.3 is 3 tenths. 3 tenths = 30 hundredths = 0.30. A 0 at the end does not change the value, so Mia is right.

items.q: A board 1 meter long is cut into 10 equal pieces. Isabella uses 4 pieces. How many meters of board does she use?
items.e: Each piece is 110 of a meter. 4 pieces = 410 = 0.4 m.

items.q: A trail has a sign every tenth of a mile. Zoe walks past the 1-mile sign and then 3 more signs. How far has she walked?
items.e: 1 mile, then 3 tenths more: 1 + 0.3 = 1.3 miles. Each sign is 0.1 mile, not 0.01.

items.q: A rope is 0.6 meter long. Elijah adds a piece that is 0.08 meter long. How long is the rope now?
items.e: 0.6 = 60100. Then 60100 + 8100 = 68100 = 0.68 m. The 8 is hundredths, so it goes in the second place.
